question.text: Benzene carbaldehyde is reacted with conc. <math> <mrow> <mtext>NaOH</mtext></mrow> </math> solution to give the products <math> <mrow> <mtext>AB</mtext></mrow> </math>. The product <math> <mtext>A</mtext> </math> can be used as a food preservative and the product <math> <mtext>B</mtext> </math> is an aromatic hydroxy compound, where <math> <mrow> <mo>−</mo><mtext>OH</mtext></mrow> </math> group is linked to <math> <mrow> <msup> <mrow> <mtext>sp</mtext></mrow> <mtext>3</mtext> </msup> </mrow> </math>-hybridised C-atom next to benzene ring. The products <math> <mtext>A</mtext> </math> and <math> <mtext>B</mtext> </math> respectively are

solution.text: When benzene carbaldehyde reacts with NaOH, it proceeds via Cannizzaro reaction. It is a disproportionation reaction in which half of the molecules of aldehyde are oxidised to carboxylate state and other half are reduced to alcohol state.
